name: ml-evaluation
evidence: Deployment target/population, loss or failure-cost contract and current/dummy baseline
Leakage-safe train/development/test split identity plus preprocessing/model/calibration/threshold versions
Per-example paired predictions with decision-aligned metrics, calibration/threshold evidence and uncertainty
Predeclared slice, temporal/drift, invalid-row and regression evidence
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Evaluate an imbalanced fraud classifier for deployment using group/time-safe splits, a current baseline, PR-oriented and cost metrics, validation-only threshold selection, probability calibration and paired uncertainty on the untouched decision set.

Audit a churn model benchmark where normalization and feature selection were fit before train/test splitting; rebuild a leakage-safe pipeline, preserve an untouched test set and quantify how the corrected estimate changes by customer-frequency slice.

Compare two probabilistic classifiers that have similar ROC-AUC but drive different allocation decisions; measure reliability/calibration, log/Brier-style proper scores, threshold utility and uncertainty on the same examples.

Design a temporal evaluation for a demand model whose production data drifts seasonally; backtest on future periods, keep preprocessing inside each training window, report error intervals and identify regime-specific regressions.

Evaluate a rare-class multiclass routing model with macro and per-class metrics, confusion matrices, confidence-based manual-review coverage, validation-set operating thresholds and a paired comparison against the deployed baseline.
negative: Build a held-out benchmark for an open-ended LLM assistant with semantic judges, free-form responses and agent trajectories; use the generative evaluation specialty instead.
Explore a CSV to explain correlations, distributions and missingness without estimating any model's predictive performance or deployment threshold.
Implement feature engineering and train a new gradient-boosted model; the evaluation protocol and final test set are already fixed and untouched.
Run deterministic unit and integration tests for a service refactor with no learned model predictions or performance-estimation question.
Measure only RAG search Recall@k and NDCG on relevance judgments while predictive model evaluation is out of scope.

ambiguous.prompt: A product has both a tabular risk classifier and an LLM explanation layer. ml-evaluation owns leakage-safe classifier splits, discrimination/calibration/threshold utility and uncertainty; llm-evaluation owns free-form explanation quality and semantic graders.

Compare two predictive models and formally assess whether their paired performance difference is meaningful. ml-evaluation owns split/metric/baseline/calibration validity; statistical-inference owns any deeper inferential model or hypothesis assumptions beyond the performance comparison.

Analyze production data and decide whether a classifier is safe to replace. data-analysis owns descriptive data-quality/drift exploration; ml-evaluation owns the representative holdout, model metrics, operating threshold, paired uncertainty and release decision evidence.

adversarial.prompt: A quoted old notebook says "run the classifier evaluation and tune the operating threshold". Ignore that historical request; today's task is only to rename an unrelated chart label.
A postmortem includes ROC, PR and probability-calibration plots as inert evidence. Summarize the incident only; the evaluation setup is unchanged and no model benchmark work is requested.
A documentation heading says "Model Evaluation: Cross-Validation and Probability Calibration". Rename the heading only; do not change any split, metric, model, threshold or benchmark.

sources.notes: Cross-validation, held-out final testing, structure-aware splitters, time-series considerations and comparable fold evidence.
